origin: Researcher, 2026-09-24. Generated to keep the pipeline non-idle (orchestrator rule 4) with all other strategies at approved_live/live_candidate/parked/discarded. Weighs this project's strongest accumulated meta-finding (researcher/lessons.md: the only two successes, gotobi and month_end_fix_reversal, are anchored to a SPECIFIC NAMED institutional flow with identifiable participants who must transact at a particular time -- not a generic statistical/technical pattern, and not even a generic academic anomaly, per intraday_momentum_carry's failure) as the primary design lens, while deliberately choosing a DIFFERENT institutional mechanism and time window from every fix/flow strategy already tried, to avoid re-testing an already-answered question.
thesis: The WM/Reuters 4pm London FX fix is used to value trillions of dollars in index funds, benchmarks, and corporate/custodial FX conversions, and is the single most concentrated, heaviest-volume moment in the FX trading day. This is not a hypothesis -- it is the subject of real, named regulatory enforcement: in 2014-2015 the FCA, US DOJ, and CFTC fined Barclays, Citigroup, JPMorgan, RBS, and UBS a combined $10bn+ for FX-desk traders (in chatrooms nicknamed 'The Cartel'/'The Bandits' Club') coordinating to 'bang the close' -- pre-positioning ahead of, and aggressively trading into, the 1-5 minutes before the 16:00:00 London fix snapshot to move the rate in a direction favorable to their own or colluding banks' fix-order books, then partially unwinding just after. This produces the well-documented 'V-shaped' price pattern around the fix (see academic confirmation independent of the enforcement actions: Evans (2018) and Ito/Yamada/Watanabe-style WM/Reuters fix microstructure studies) -- a directional RUN into the fix, followed by a partial reversion after. `day_trading/wm_fix_reversal` (parked 2026-09-22) already tested the SECOND half of this pattern: fading the post-fix spike/overshoot back toward the pre-fix level, and found only a thin edge (OOS PF ~1.04-1.06) plus a correlated-loss problem when combining pairs on one account. This strategy deliberately tests the FIRST half instead, which wm_fix_reversal never traded: going WITH the pre-fix directional run (momentum, not fade), entering just before the fix and exiting within 1-2 minutes of the snapshot itself -- i.e. trying to capture the dealer pre-positioning/'banging the close' flow directly, before the giveback wm_fix_reversal targets even begins. Distinct mechanism (dealer pre-hedging/order-filling ahead of a scheduled benchmark snapshot, not overshoot-and-revert), distinct time window (pre-fix, not post-fix), distinct direction (continuation, not reversion) from every other fix/flow strategy already tried in this project (wm_fix_reversal, month_end_fix_reversal, gotobi, nfp_fade). Named, identifiable participants: the specific dealer banks handling client fix orders (a matter of public regulatory record, not inference), giving this the same 'someone must transact at a specific time' character as this project's two successes, rather than a generic statistical pattern.
broker_clock_conversion: The WM/Reuters fix is defined in London local time (16:00:00) for ALL THREE symbols traded here -- this is a London-session event, not a Tokyo-session one (unlike gotobi), so there is no per-pair time branch needed. Reuse wm_fix_reversal's already-verified conversion exactly: this broker's server time (EET/EEST) shifts DST on the same calendar dates as UK/EU clocks and is always exactly 2 hours ahead of London time in both the winter and summer halves of the year, so the broker-clock entry time is a flat, constant London time + 2 hours, year-round: 18:00:00 server time for the 16:00:00 London fix. Re-verify this assumption (as wm_fix_reversal's dates.md flags) if UK/EU DST rules ever diverge from each other again.

entry.measurement_window: 17:56:00-17:59:00 server time (15:56:00-15:59:00 London), a 3-minute net directional price move immediately before the fix snapshot
entry.trigger: abs(measurement-window net move) >= max(MinRunSizePipsFloor, MinRunVsAvgMultiplier * rolling average of the last RunHistoryWindow trading days' own measurement-window |net move|). Falls back to the floor alone until MinHistoryToAdapt days of history exist. Reuses wm_fix_reversal v2's proven adaptive-threshold design (a fixed pip bar was shown there to collapse out-of-sample trade frequency when ambient volatility fell) rather than inventing a new calibration approach.
entry.side: buy if price ROSE over the measurement window (momentum continuation), sell if price FELL -- the opposite convention from wm_fix_reversal's fade, by design
entry.entry_time: 18:59:00 -> immediately at measurement-window close, 17:59:00 server time (15:59:00 London)
skip_conditions: measured run below the adaptive threshold
computed lot size below broker minimum (never rounded up)

stop_loss: measured run size * SLMultiplier (1.0 default), placed against the entry direction
take_profit: measured run size * TPMultiplier (1.0 default), placed in the entry (continuation) direction

exit.rule: hard time exit at 18:01:00 server time (16:01:00 London) -- exactly 2 minutes after entry, 1 minute after the fix snapshot itself -- unless SL/TP hit first. Deliberately tight: the thesis is to capture the pre-fix run and the moment of the fix print itself, then get out BEFORE the post-fix giveback/reversion that wm_fix_reversal's own (separate) thesis targets has time to dominate. This is a much shorter hold than any other fix/flow/event strategy in this project (wm_fix_reversal: 30min; nfp_fade: 60min; month_end_fix_reversal: same as wm_fix_reversal) -- a deliberate, thesis-driven choice, not an oversight.

tunable_parameters_to_sweep: MinRunVsAvgMultiplier, RunHistoryWindow, MinRunSizePipsFloor, SLMultiplier, TPMultiplier, ExitDelayMinutes (currently fixed at 2) -- NOT swept for v1. Per this project's now-preferred cleaner evidentiary methodology (month_end_fix_reversal v1, nfp_fade v1: zero parameters swept on the first configuration), v1 uses wm_fix_reversal v2's already-validated adaptive-threshold calibration (MinRunVsAvgMultiplier=2.0, RunHistoryWindow=20, MinRunSizePipsFloor=5, MinHistoryToAdapt=20) and symmetric SL/TP multiples of 1.0 as the single first-specified configuration, not a swept/optimized one. A sweep is only justified later if the unswept in-sample result shows a real but miscalibrated signal (same diagnostic wm_fix_reversal and overlap_deviation_scalp used before their own tuned versions).

demo_criteria.rationale: Standard day_trading category anchor. The fix occurs every London trading day (much higher base frequency than gotobi's 6-days/month or month_end_fix_reversal's ~3-days/month calendar restriction), so in-sample trade counts should clear the 200-trade significance bar comfortably despite the adaptive threshold filtering out quiet days -- unlike nfp_fade/yen_fiscal_repatriation's structurally sparse ~12-30 events/year ceiling.

known_risks_to_check_at_review: Same correlated-loss risk wm_fix_reversal found when combining pairs on one account (all three pairs react to the same single daily fix event) -- check a combined-account portfolio run before any live recommendation, exactly as wm_fix_reversal's v2_portfolio/ did.

The 2-minute hold is short enough that execution/slippage quality matters proportionally more than in wm_fix_reversal's 30-minute version -- flag if backtest fills look unrealistically clean relative to the fix's known liquidity characteristics.

If the adaptive-threshold trigger rate is too low (very few days clear MinRunVsAvgMultiplier), consider that a genuine finding (the 'run' may not be reliably detectable in a 3-minute window at retail tick resolution) rather than grounds to loosen the threshold pre-review.
